Mobile Experience — Design vs Dev Comparison

Dev URL: https://app.eg-dev.ai (mobile 390px viewport)

Date: June 29, 2026

Total

How to read: Gap = mismatch OR hard-coded value where token should be used, Match = correct value AND uses token-backed class, Verify = needs code inspection to confirm token usage (not just value match).

Executive Summary — Top Issues

Ordered by user-facing severity. Items marked ★ are compliance or accessibility risks.

  1. ★ Login page doesn't scroll — overflow: hidden on html/body clips legal disclaimers mid-sentence. Users cannot read required compliance text.
  2. ★ Continue button stays enabled on empty input — Should be disabled (Hemlock disabled state) until a valid email is entered.
  3. Rich content cards don't stack on mobile — Multi-column comparison grids overflow at 390px; text hard-clips ("New Hampshir"). Should be single-column stacked cards.
  4. Visible horizontal scrollbar on tables — Native scrollbar appears on data tables; should be hidden (CSS scrollbar-width: none).
  5. Thinking status text duplicates — "Formulating response…" appears multiple times stacked. Design shows ONE replaceable text line below dots.
  6. Systemic: hard-coded hex values instead of tokens — border-[#DCD8CB], text-[#2D2926], placeholder-[#A8A49E], shadow-[…] appear across 12+ elements. Should use semantic token classes.
  7. Continue button styling doesn't match Hemlock — Wrong bg (#3C3C3C vs #0E0E0E), wrong text (#FFF vs #EEEDEB), wrong font-size (14 vs 16), left-aligned (should be centered).
  8. Holding detail: circular letter avatar instead of rounded-square image — Design uses a 36×36 rounded-square image fill with cornerRadius: $O:radius-2xs; app renders a circle with a letter inside.
  9. Holding detail: title truncated instead of wrapping — Name shows ellipsis ("Vanguard Tot…"); design uses two-line vertical layout (ticker code above, full name below) with fill_container width to allow wrapping.
  10. Holding detail: padding/spacing completely off — Section gaps, row padding, and container insets in the holding detail popup don't match design tokens. Text in the detail rows isn't wrapping — it truncates or overflows instead of respecting fill_container width.

Each comparison item (Florida, Georgia, etc.) gets its own full-width card stacked vertically. Gap

Inconsistent overflow handling All content should handle overflow consistently openui-table uses scroll indicator (">"); comparison cards just clip Unify overflow behavior — all wide content should use the same scroll pattern with visible indicator Gap
Text truncation without ellipsis Text should always wrap on mobile — never truncate or clip "New Hampshire" APPEARS hard-clipped in the screenshot, but this is caused by the card grid overflow + scrollbar (not a text truncation issue). Once cards stack to single-column, text will have room to wrap naturally. Fix is the card-grid stacking above — once cards are full-width, text wraps. No separate truncation fix needed. Gap
AI heading typography Headings should fit within 320px content width without issues "State Tax Code Comparison — 2026" heading fits but uses large bold text — acceptable — Match
AI paragraph text wrapping Text wraps naturally within message width Body text wraps correctly within container — Match
Data table (State/Structure) scroll Table should be scrollable when wider than panel Has ">" chevron affordance indicating horizontal scroll works — Match
Visible horizontal scrollbar on tables Scrollbars should be hidden AND the content frame should not exceed the panel width in the first place — tables should fit within 390px or use a controlled scroll container without a visible scrollbar Visible tan scrollbar appears at bottom of table sections. Root cause: the table/frame is wider than the chat panel (390px), creating overflow. The scrollbar then appears because overflow-x is auto with no scrollbar hiding. Two fixes needed: (1) Constrain table max-width to the panel width so it does not overflow at all when possible, or use responsive column hiding. (2) When overflow IS necessary, hide the native scrollbar via scrollbar-width: none / ::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none } while keeping swipe gesture support. Gap
